findings.issue_text: Crash (TypeError) in EventManager.ts:117-118 on the Google Meet fallback when no destination calendar exists: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` guards the destructuring but not the property access, so when destinationCalendar is null or [], `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a 500 (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`), hitting exactly the 'Google Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' scenario — reachable because handleNewBooking.ts explicitly assigns `destinationCalendar: null` and confirm.handler.ts assigns `[]`; TypeScript won't catch it without `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`

Dead fallback in Google CalendarService.ts updateEvent (:254-257) and deleteEvent (:314-317): the `find()` predicate compares every calendar's externalId against a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it can never match and the expression always evaluates to undefined; the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback is now dead code, so bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings plus new bookings created through the no-credentialId destination branch without externalId) update/delete against undefined or 'primary' via defaultCalendarId — leaving rescheduled Google events at the old time (external double-booking) and ghost events after cancellation

Non-Google calendar services (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:70-78, larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128-130 and :162-164, CalDAV CalendarService.ts:156-166) ignore the per-host destination and still derive the target from `destinationCalendar[0]`, so for a COLLECTIVE event with two hosts on the same non-Google integration, host B's createEvent runs with B's credential but targets host A's externalId, failing and being swallowed as success:false — host B's calendar never receives the booking while a reference row is still written pointing at a nonexistent event, and the per-destination loop in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents is only correct for Google

EventManager.update (:~510-530) calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` with `credential === undefined` when the reference's credentialId matches neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor a DB row (e.g., a team host deleted their calendar app): `CalendarManager.updateEvent` immediately dereferences a property on undefined via `getCalendar(credential)`, and the resulting TypeError caught by the outer catch fails ALL calendar references for that booking, not just the stale one — createAllCalendarEvents got an `if (credential)` guard in this PR but the update path did not

Errors in EventManager.update (:~593-608) are now completely swallowed: the catch block removed `console.error(message)`, the message string is built but never used, and nothing else logs, so any throw inside update (TypeError, Prisma errors, etc.) returns failure rows — or `[]` if calendarReference was never assigned, which can read as 'nothing to update' — with zero trace in logs, leaving operators no signal that a reschedule failed to touch external calendars

The two new fetch-credential-from-DB fallbacks construct credentials inconsistently: EventManager.ts (:~344-360, :~505-525) builds `{ appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug ?? "", id, type, key, ... }` while handleCancelBooking.ts (:~427-437) assigns the raw `prisma.credential.findUnique()` record with no appName — if getCalendar routes on appName the handleCancelBooking variant yields an undefined calendar and silently no-ops so team hosts' calendar events survive cancellation, and if getCalendar falls back to credential.type the EventManager variant's hyphenated app slug ('google-calendar' vs the 'google_calendar' convention used elsewhere) mis-routes, leaving `CalendarManager.createEvent` returning success: true when calendar is undefined and storing a reference for an event never created; the two paths cannot both be correct

loadUsers (handleNewBooking.ts:~724-762) swallows the specific failure reasons it just introduced: the new `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` and `throw new Error("eventType.hosts is not properly defined.")` are thrown inside the try, so the catch converts them into a generic 500 'Unable to load users' — the descriptive messages never reach the client and nothing is logged; additionally an empty dynamicUserList, which previously flowed into normal no-users handling, is now a hard 500, and Prisma known-errors are rethrown as 400s with raw Prisma messages

Crash on booking creation in EventManager.ts:117-119: new code destructures evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] into mainHostDestinationCalendar and dereferences .integration without a guard, so Google-Meet-location bookings by users with null/empty destinationCalendar (set to null in handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1068) throw a TypeError and fail the entire booking; old optional-chaining code gracefully fell back to Cal Video

Inverted condition in organization create.handler.ts:150-153: old code (!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) writes slug only when billing is disabled, but new code (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}) writes slug only when billing is enabled — enabling slug squatting past the requestedSlug verification gate on hosted deployments and leaving self-hosted organizations with no slug at all (also an unrelated change to the PR's purpose)

Missing ownership validation on credential fetch in EventManager createAllCalendarEvents (~346-364) and updateAllCalendarEvents (~505-530) plus handleCancelBooking.ts (~430-443): credentials are loaded directly by id via prisma.credential.findUnique with no verification they belong to the booking's organizer/hosts/team, removing the implicit ownership check previously provided by this.calendarCredentials — a latent IDOR allowing attacker-influenced credentialIds to direct calendar writes and OAuth token use against arbitrary users' accounts

Dead fallback in Google CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent (255-256, ~314-317): the find() in externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the comparison can never match and the fallback always yields undefined (old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId) — bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId fail to update/delete, leaving stale events after reschedules and events remaining on hosts' calendars after cancellation

Non-Google calendar services (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76, larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128,164,192,237, lib/CalendarService.ts:156-166) always use destinationCalendar[0] instead of the destination matching the credential — for collective events with multiple hosts, services invoked with host B's credential target host A's externalId, so events for non-Google members are silently created on the wrong calendar or not created at all

handleCancelBooking.ts (~432-446) DB-fallback credential lacks appName: unlike the EventManager paths it assigns the raw prisma.credential row to calendarCredential, so getCalendar() resolves no service and returns null, making calendar?.deleteEvent a no-op — canceling a collective booking leaves events on non-organizer hosts' calendars

One unresolvable reference poisons all calendar updates in EventManager updateAllCalendarEvents (~515-535): if a reference.credentialId can't be resolved, updateEvent(undefined, ...) throws inside the try and jumps to catch, aborting updates for remaining references and discarding results of already-performed ones, leaving booking references stale while remote events were mutated — each reference should be handled independently

Sequential per-host calendar event creation in `createAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~339–362`) replaces the previous parallel `Promise.all` execution, so external API round trips (Google/O365 insert, `getCalendar()` construction, possible OAuth token refresh) now run strictly serially, making booking-creation latency grow linearly with host count (a 5-host collective event can add multiple seconds of serial provider API latency with timeout risk); parallelize across destinations or document the sequencing rationale.

N+1 credential lookup inside the destination loop in `createAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~344`): `prisma.credential.findUnique` executes once per non-organizer host destination whose credential isn't in `this.calendarCredentials`, on every booking, serially compounding latency; batch with a single `prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })` or hydrate all host credentials up front in the caller.

Fetched credentials are never merged back into `this.calendarCredentials` in `createAllCalendarEvents`, so the same credential rows are re-fetched again in `updateAllCalendarEvents` for the same booking.

Duplicate event creation when multiple destinations lack `credentialId` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~364–369`): the else branch runs `Promise.all` over all `this.calendarCredentials` of that integration per destination, so multiple hosts with credentialId-less destination calendars of the same integration produce M×N inserts and user-visible duplicate events on the same calendar, wasting provider API quota.

N+1 credential lookup per calendar reference on update in `updateAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~505–535`): `prisma.credential.findUnique` is awaited inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, one sequential DB query per reference on every reschedule; batchable with a single `findMany`.

N+1 credential lookup per reference on cancel in `handleCancelBooking.ts:~427`: the new per-reference loop adds `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, one query per teammate-host reference whose credential isn't in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`; batchable with one `findMany`.

Dead fallback breaks Google Calendar update/delete for bookings without `externalCalendarId` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~256` in `updateEvent` and `~314–316` in `deleteEvent`): in the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match and the expression always yields `undefined`, unlike the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`; updates/deletes for pre-refactor bookings and no-credentialId-path bookings issue API calls with an undefined `calendarId` and fail, stranding or duplicating calendar events.

TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty in `create` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts:~117`): `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructure yields `undefined`, then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws where the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was null-safe; reachable when a Meet-location event is created for a user with no destination calendar, causing booking creation to 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Unrelated conditional flip in org creation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:~151`): `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the polarity so that when billing is disabled, orgs are now created with no `slug` at all.

EventManager.create crashes with a TypeError on empty/missing destinationCalendar because optional chaining was removed: destructuring `[]`/`null` yields `undefined` and the code reads `.integration` off it directly, so Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar (set to `null` in handleNewBooking.ts:1067 and `[]` in confirm.handler.ts:175, paypal-webhook.ts:152, webhook.ts:119) throw a 500 at booking create/confirm/payment-success instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback predicate is tautologically dead: in the `else` branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match, making `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` always `undefined` and causing googleapis 'Missing required parameters: calendarId' errors — breaking reschedule/cancel of any booking whose stored reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (legacy and new fallback-created references), leaving stale/orphaned events and double-booked calendars.

Organization creation slug condition is inverted in create.handler.ts:151: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` is the incorrect rewrite of `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, so when team billing is disabled orgs are created with no slug at all (breaking org URLs/API lookups), and when enabled orgs get a direct `slug` immediately, bypassing the `requestedSlug`-until-payment billing gate.

Video booking references lose their credentialId: the non-calendar half of the ternary in EventManager.ts:169-170 changed from `result.credentialId` (the Zoom/Teams credential) to `undefined`, so every new booking's `_video` reference stores `credentialId: null`, breaking credential-based video-meeting deletion on cancel and `deleteCredentialHandler` matching, orphaning video meetings or picking the wrong credential when a user has multiple video integrations.

Breaking, unversioned schema drift in BOOKING_* webhook payloads: the `destinationCalendar` field changed from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[]`, so external webhook subscribers reading `payload.destinationCalendar?.integration`/`.externalId` now get `undefined` and silently misroute or crash, with no versioning, migration note, or compatibility period.

Breaking change to exported `@calcom/types` public interfaces: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is now an array and `Calendar.createEvent` now takes a required second `credentialId` argument, breaking out-of-tree consumers of the shared package (app-store packages, self-hosted forks, community apps) with no deprecation alias, minor-version framing, adapter, or migration note.

Destinations without a credentialId are broken end-to-end: Google's `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` never matches in the fallback branch, so events are silently created on `'primary'` instead of the user's configured destination calendar, and `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the new `externalId` param so the stored booking reference has `externalCalendarId: null` — making these bookings created on the wrong calendar and impossible to update/delete by reference.

Multi-host destination selection is Google-only: O365/Lark/CalDAV createEvent implementations ignore the per-host `credentialId`, so createAllCalendarEvents' new per-destination loop writes duplicate events on the organizer's calendar (destinationCalendar[0]) and none on members' calendars, while per-destination references point at calendars with no event, causing 404s on update/delete.

EventManager.update error path now resolves with `[]` instead of a failure result: if the `try` throws before `calendarReference` is assigned (e.g., booking lookup failure), the catch resolves with `[]`, which is indistinguishable from 'nothing to update'; callers checking `results.some(r => !r.success)` treat total update failure as success, leaving stale calendar events after reschedule.

Collective members' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none: handleNewBooking.ts:1067 sets `destinationCalendar: null` (not `[]`), so the optional-chained `push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` at handleNewBooking.ts:1075-1077 is a no-op and every member's collected destination calendar is discarded, defeating the PR's headline feature for exactly those collective bookings.

Stale `credential` leaks across the reference loop in EventManager.update: `credential` is declared once outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop but only conditionally assigned inside it, so if a later reference's credential is not in `calendarCredentials` and the DB fetch returns null, the previous iteration's credential is retained and `updateEvent` runs with the wrong host's credential, throwing and marking all references failed or updating through an unrelated credential.

Null dereference in packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty (destructuring yields undefined), crashing booking creation for Meet-location bookings without a destination calendar; same crash reachable from confirm.handler.ts and Stripe/PayPal webhooks, leaving paid bookings stuck and causing endless provider retries

Dead-code fallback in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~256) and deleteEvent (~315): the fallback find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match because externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, yielding calendarId: undefined, so bookings without a stored externalCalendarId (legacy or no-credentialId path) fail to reschedule or cancel on Google and external events get stuck/orphaned

Unguarded updateEvent(credential, ...) in packages/core/EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (~525-540) after failed credential resolution: getCalendar(undefined) throws when the reference's credential is missing (deleted credential or missing app slug), turning a single disconnected credential into a total reschedule failure for every reference

All-or-nothing failure across calendar references in packages/core/EventManager.ts (~493-560): per-reference updateEvent promises are awaited together via Promise.all, so one host's API failure (revoked token, 404, deleted event) rejects the whole batch and marks every reference success: false, discarding updates that succeeded on other hosts and causing DB/external-calendar desync

Exception swallowing with zero logging in packages/core/EventManager.ts catch block (~593-607): the console.error(message) was removed with no replacement logger.error, so reschedule failures surface only as silent success: false with no log of the root exception, making production desyncs undebuggable

Multi-host support only implemented for Google: packages/app-store/larkcalendar, office365calendar CalendarServices and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts ignore the new credentialId parameter and always use destinationCalendar[0], so for host B these providers build a URL/calendarId from host A's externalId using B's token, causing API errors and silently missing calendar events for collective bookings on all non-Google providers

Events silently created in the wrong calendar when destination has no credentialId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145-150 + packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:264-267): the find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) matches nothing and falls back to "primary" of every matching credential (duplicate events across credentials), and CalendarManager.createEvent returns the passed-in externalId unconditionally, persisting an undefined/mismatched BookingReference.externalCalendarId

Merge-delete path in packages/core/EventManager.ts (~553) still uses find (single reference) instead of filter, so reschedule-merge of a multi-reference collective booking only deletes the first host's old calendar event, leaving stale events for other hosts at the old time

Recurring-cancellation block in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts (~427-455) duplicated per reference: the allRemainingBookings deletion loop now sits inside the for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) loop, running N times for multi-reference bookings (repeated event deletion, 404/410 noise, rate-limit pressure), and still iterates the organizer's credentials rather than each reference's credentialId

Video booking references lose their credentialId in packages/core/EventManager.ts (~169): credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined drops the association between the stored meeting and the video credential that created it, so any flow resolving the video credential via reference.credentialId will misbehave or silently skip

loadUsers catch in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts (~744-757) misclassifies server-side Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError as a 400 client error, converts the deliberate dynamicUserList error into an opaque 500, and never logs the original error, losing root causes and correct status codes for monitoring

Member destination calendars silently dropped in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts (~1073-1075): evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) no-ops when the organizer/eventType destinationCalendar is null, so for COLLECTIVE events where only members have destination calendars their calendars are silently excluded

Sequential, unbounded external calls in packages/core/EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents (~340-360): createEvent is awaited per destination inside a for...of with no Promise.all and no timeout on external API calls, so a single hung calendar API call blocks the entire booking request indefinitely and latency grows linearly with host count on collective events

Inverted condition in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-154: the guard `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was flipped to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` — the opposite condition. Slug is now assigned immediately when team billing is enabled (bypassing the requestedSlug/verification flow) and no slug at all is written when billing is disabled; this out-of-scope change breaks org-creation semantics.

Dead/broken fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent (~254-256) and deleteEvent (~314-317): `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — the find() branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, then searches for cal.externalId === undefined/null which can never match, so the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback is effectively deleted and calendarId is passed as undefined to the Google API; bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings, and new bookings via the no-credentialId path) now fail to update/delete their Google event.

Multi-host support is implemented only for Google; every non-Google service (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76, larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127-128/163-164, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-166/509-514) collapses to `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses only entry [0], while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination with its own credential — so for a collective booking with hosts on O365/Apple/Lark, the second host's call either 404s (writing host A's calendar ID through host B's credential) or no-ops; the Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId) interface param (types/Calendar.d.ts:221) is honored only by Google.

Organizer email no longer corresponds to the calendar the event is written to (Google CalendarService createEvent:122-126, updateEvent:~228-232): the organizer email is derived from destinationCalendar[0].externalId while the insert/update targets the credentialId-matched destination, so when creating host B's copy of a collective event the payload claims host A's calendar ID as organizer while writing to host B's calendar; it should use the same credential-matched entry as selectedCalendar.

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar became an array but only [0] is persisted on the booking (handleNewBooking.ts:1871-1875 connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id`): every consumer that reconstructs the event from the DB (cancel, reschedule, reminder, webhooks — all the [booking.destinationCalendar] wrapping sites in this diff) sees a one-element array while handleNewBooking built a multi-element one, so the data model and the runtime shape have permanently diverged invisibly to consumers.

Legacy destinations without credentialId now create on 'primary' and store no externalCalendarId (Google CalendarService.ts:145-151, CalendarManager.ts:230-236, EventManager.ts ~365 else-branch): old behavior used destinationCalendar.externalId (the user's explicitly chosen calendar), but the new code matches by credentialId and otherwise falls back to 'primary' — for DestinationCalendar rows with null credentialId, the event lands in the account's primary calendar, and since externalId isn't passed in that branch the stored reference has no externalCalendarId, so reschedule/cancel of those bookings loses calendar sync.

handleCancelBooking.ts:~427-437 DB credential fallback omits appName needed by getCalendar: unlike the two EventManager copies (which include app.slug and map appName), this third hand-rolled copy does a bare prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } }) and assigns the raw Credential to calendarCredential, then calls getCalendar(calendarCredential) which requires appName to select the service — likely yielding a null calendar and the delete being silently skipped.

Recurring-event deletion now runs once per reference, causing duplicate deletes (handleCancelBooking.ts:~447-470): the recurring branch (iterate all user credentials × updated bookings) is now inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, so for a multi-host collective booking every updated booking's event gets deleted N times, with the inner logic still using .find (first reference only); the recurring cleanup should be owned once by the outer loop, not multiplied.

Video references silently lose credentialId (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~166-169): the first reference-mapping block changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `... : undefined`, so for non-calendar (video) results the video app's credential id is no longer recorded, while the second block (~line 208) still stores result.credentialId — the two blocks are now inconsistent, and downstream flows that locate bookings by reference credentialId (e.g., credential uninstall cleanup) will miss video meetings.

The new externalId parameter on CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:221, 264-265) is dead weight: it never influences creation and is only echoed into the EventResult, while the service independently re-derives the target calendar from credentialId — two sources of truth for where the event landed; if a provider's internal derivation ever diverges (e.g., the 'primary' fallback), the persisted reference describes a calendar the event isn't in.
When the DB credential fetch in createAllCalendarEvents fails, the destination is skipped with no logging — a host's calendar silently misses the event.

Copy-pasted destination-wrapping ternary across 8+ call sites (bookingReminder.ts:107/130, webhook.ts:101/229, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156, confirm.handler.ts:175-179, editLocation.handler.ts:85-89, deleteCredential.handler.ts:290-294, handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255/528-532, requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-243): the `booking.dc ? [booking.dc] : user.dc ? [user.dc] : []` pattern is duplicated with drifting variations (some end in [], handleNewBooking ends in null, requestReschedule drops the user fallback entirely, preserving the old `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` typo's behavior); it should be a single shared helper like getBookingDestinationCalendars(booking).

In handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1071, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` no-ops when destinationCalendar is null (organizer and event type both DC-less), so members' calendars collected into teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded instead of becoming the value.

In handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1071, the collective destination assembly is asymmetric: when eventType.destinationCalendar is set, the organizer's personal calendar is excluded while members' calendars are pushed.

The loadUsers rewrite (handleNewBooking.ts:~724-755) is unrelated scope creep that drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user query and converts all failures into generic 400/500 HttpErrors — it should be reverted out of this PR or verified that nothing downstream reads user.organization.

In `EventManager.create` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts` ~line 117), destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when the array is null or empty, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when the location is Google Meet — bookings with Meet location and no destination calendar now return 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video (regression of a previously-safe path using `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`).

In Google `updateEvent` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` ~lines 253-256), the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is dead code because `externalCalendarId` is falsy in the else branch, so `find` can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined — `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, silently breaking reschedule/location-edit for any booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.

In Google `deleteEvent` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` ~lines 312-315), the same dead-code fallback yields `calendarId: undefined` when `externalCalendarId` is missing, so cancelled bookings leave orphaned events on users' real Google calendars, and depending on how `apiDeletes` is awaited a rejected promise may fail the whole cancel flow.

In Google `createEvent` (`CalendarService.ts` ~146-152) combined with EventManager's createAllCalendarEvents else-branch, legacy destination calendars with nullable `credentialId` never match `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, silently falling back to `calendarId: "primary"` — events are created on the wrong calendar while the stored reference gets `externalCalendarId: null`, routing later updates/deletes into the broken fallbacks; creation reports success while the real destination is wrong, and `organizer.email` is set to the legacy destination calendar's externalId which no longer matches the actual target calendar.

In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` ~148-152, the feature-flag condition is inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses the previous behavior — with billing enabled the slug is claimed immediately bypassing the requested-slug verification flow, and with billing disabled no slug is set at all (likely a required-field Prisma error breaking org creation on self-hosted). This unrelated hunk silently reverses an intentional behavior.

In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (`packages/core/EventManager.ts` ~493-520), the `credential` variable is declared outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop and retains the previous reference's credential when a reference's `credentialId` resolves to a deleted credential — host B's update runs with host A's calendar credential (wrong calendar or 404/403); on the first iteration `credential` is `undefined` and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` throws into the outer catch, which returns all references as failed while already-launched update promises keep running, causing partial state divergence.

Non-Google calendar services only honor `destinationCalendar[0]`, breaking multi-host collective events for Lark/Office365/CalDAV: `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~128, ~164, ~192, ~237) and `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~72-76) use the first element as `calendarId`/`eventsUrl`, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (~156-166) filters to `externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` — in EventManager's per-destination loop, host B's credential is invoked with host A's calendar, causing API errors or silent no-ops so host B silently gets no event.

In Google create/update (`CalendarService.ts` ~119-126 and ~225-230), `organizer.email` is forced to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (host A's) while `selectedCalendar` is found via credentialId — the two lookups diverge exactly in the multi-host scenario, so the event lands on host B's calendar claiming host A's calendar email as organizer, which Google may reject or misattribute.

Deferred-creation flows only ever see the first host's destination calendar: `handleNewBooking.ts` ~1871-1877 persists only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` on the booking, and rebuild paths (`confirm.handler.ts` ~175, `paypal-webhook.ts` ~150, `payments/api/webhook.ts` ~119/~229, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`) construct the event from that single stored row — for collective multi-host bookings requiring confirmation or payment, hosts 2..N never get calendar events at all.

In `handleCancelBooking.ts` ~418-450, the recurring-deletion branch (`recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings`) now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so with N calendar references every deletion is enqueued N times and attempted with every calendar credential regardless of match — producing 404 noise, wasted API quota, and potential poisoning of the `apiDeletes` aggregation; the recurring handling should run once, not per reference.

In `loadUsers` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` ~724-766), `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined...")` is thrown inside the try and caught by `catch (error)`, then re-thrown as `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"` — a client-input validation problem returns 500 instead of the intended 400; conversely, `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` messages are surfaced verbatim to the API client as 400s, leaking internal Prisma details.

`loadUsers` in `handleNewBooking.ts` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the user select, so any downstream consumer of `user.organization.slug` in the booking flow now receives `undefined`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` changes the `organization.create` payload from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which is a direct inversion of when `slug` is persisted. This means when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, `slug` is no longer written at all, and when it is true, `slug` is written immediately (while `metadata.requestedSlug` is still conditionally set for the enabled case). From the diff alone, this is a concrete behavioral change to org creation and is consistent with the finding that the guard was flipped and could break expected semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/broken fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent (~254-256) and deleteEvent (~314-317): `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — the find() branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, then searches for cal.externalId === undefined/null which can never match, so the old destinationCalendar.externalId fallback is effectively deleted and calendarId is passed as undefined to the Google API; bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings, and new bookings via the no-credentialId path) now fail to update/delete their Google event.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar as:

```ts
externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

But the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), and then it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null/""`), which will typically never match a real calendar externalId. This effectively removes the previous fallback to the event’s destination calendar and can cause update/delete to target the wrong calendar (or rely on later defaults like `primary`), breaking updates/deletes for bookings whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.

This means when creating the 2nd host’s event, the service still targets host[0]’s calendarId while using host[1]’s credential, which can fail (e.g., 404/permission) or create in the wrong calendar. Additionally, the `Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId)` interface is updated, and Google implements it, but Office365/Lark signatures in the diff remain `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`, indicating incomplete/broken integration with the new multi-destination behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When the DB credential fetch in createAllCalendarEvents fails, the destination is skipped with no logging — a host's calendar silently misses the event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deferred-creation flows only ever see the first host's destination calendar: `handleNewBooking.ts` ~1871-1877 persists only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` on the booking, and rebuild paths (`confirm.handler.ts` ~175, `paypal-webhook.ts` ~150, `payments/api/webhook.ts` ~119/~229, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`) construct the event from that single stored row — for collective multi-host bookings requiring confirmation or payment, hosts 2..N never get calendar events at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over it to create events for multiple destination calendars. However, `handleNewBooking.ts` persists only the first destination calendar on the Booking (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` around ~1843-1871). adjudication_records.issue_text: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` ~418-450, the recurring-deletion branch (`recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings`) now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so with N calendar references every deletion is enqueued N times and attempted with every calendar credential regardless of match — producing 404 noise, wasted API quota, and potential poisoning of the `apiDeletes` aggregation; the recurring handling should run once, not per reference.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the code now loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`.
